label: Uneasy restraint
summary: Saturday's danger sits in one corridor. Yemen's Houthis took full control of the Red Sea coast, including Perim Island at the mouth of Bab al-Mandeb, and Saudi Arabia shut its East-West pipeline — the route built to bypass the blocked Strait of Hormuz — after drones from Iraq hit pumping stations. Riyadh declined to retaliate, giving Baghdad room to act; Iraq dismissed a commander and closed a border crossing with Iran. That restraint is the day's best news. North Korea fired ballistic missiles from Wonsan hours after allied naval drills ended, and Copernicus confirmed August was the joint-hottest month ever measured, 1.65°C above pre-industrial. Pressure eased at the margins: Wall Street snapped a four-day slide as the oil rally paused, though ten-year yields near 4.97% still point to a Fed hike. The weighted formula gave 40; no editorial adjustment.
